text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Syrian President Assad considering discussions with Israel on finding a basis for renewing negotiations.
- Prime Minister Netanyahu and Finance Minister Meridor apparently agree on budget cut of approximately 750 million shekels.
- Israeli President Weizman and Palestinian President Arafat to meet tomorrow at Erez crossing, U.S. envoy Ross delaying arrival until after the meeting.
- Strauss family to announce within two days whether it will buy controlling interest in Elite.
- Israel will announce pledge to stick to precise timetable for implementing peace deal with the Palestinians.
- Additional state budget cut will be about 700 million shekels.
- Strauss family decides to buy Elite.
- Netanyahu and Meridor decide there will not be any deviation from budget deficit despite economic slowdown.
- Industrial production stagnant since September 1996. Inflation steady at high level of seven percent.
- Government to ease Jerusalem Arab ID troubles.
- EU envoy Moratinos: Syria does want peace.
- State revenues stagnant in first four months of 1997, Meridor and Netanyahu fail to decide on added budget cut.
